explain.say: In 1206 a steppe leader called Temüjin was proclaimed Chinggis Khan, often written Genghis. Within about seventy years his family ruled from Korea to Russia and Iran, the largest connected land empire in history. Look at the timeline of how fast it grew.

explain.say: Look at the map: Beijing, Samarkand, Baghdad and Kyiv, all taken by Mongol armies. The conquests were devastating. Cities that resisted, like those of Khwarazm in Central Asia, were destroyed, and Baghdad was sacked in 1258 with huge loss of life; numbers are uncertain. Why might terror have been a deliberate strategy?

How big was it? See the sizes. About 24 million square kilometres at its height, bigger than Russia today, and nearly five times the Roman Empire. Mongol success came from superb horsemanship, discipline, rapid communication and using engineers from conquered lands. Which of these surprises you?

After conquest came the Pax Mongolica, Mongol peace. See the network. Yam relay stations carried news across Asia, and paiza, metal passes, gave safe passage to merchants and envoys like Marco Polo. Skilled people, crops, medicine and astronomy moved east and west. What else might travel on such routes?

The same routes may have helped carry the Black Death in the 1340s. Jack Weatherford praises Mongol openness; others stress the destruction, and Timothy May speaks of a Mongol exchange with both sides. Wonderful work. Challenge: weigh one benefit against one cost of Mongol rule in a single sentence.

faq.q: How big was the Mongol Empire?
faq.a: At its height, around the 1270s, about 24 million square kilometres, from Korea and China to Iran, Russia and the edge of Hungary: the largest contiguous land empire in history. By the 1260s it had split into four khanates.
asks: What was the largest land empire?

faq.a: The Mongol peace: a period in the late thirteenth and early fourteenth centuries when Mongol rule made travel and trade across Eurasia safer, helped by relay stations and passes, so goods, people and ideas moved widely.

faq.q: Why did the Mongols conquer so much?
faq.a: Skilled mounted archers, tight discipline and organisation, fast communication, flexible tactics, use of foreign engineers for sieges, and deliberate terror against cities that resisted, along with divisions among their enemies.
asks: How did Chinggis Khan rise to power?

faq.a: A network of relay stations with horses, food and lodging for official messengers and travellers, letting news cross the empire quickly. Holders of a paiza, a metal tablet, could use it.
asks: What was the Mongol postal system?

faq.q: Were the Mongols good or bad for the world?
faq.a: Historians are divided. They caused immense death and destruction, but their empire also linked Eurasia, spreading trade, technology and knowledge. Many now speak of a Mongol exchange with costs and benefits.

facts: Temüjin was proclaimed Chinggis Khan in 1206.
The Mamluks defeated a Mongol army at Ain Jalut in 1260.

quiz.say: The Mongol Empire covered about 24 million km² and the Roman Empire about 5 million. About how many times bigger was the Mongol Empire?
quiz.why: 24 divided by 5 is 4.8, so nearly 5 times.

wrong.1: Twice would be only 10 million km².
wrong.2: Twenty times would be 100 million km², more than any empire.

quiz.say: Who stopped the Mongol advance at Ain Jalut in 1260?
quiz.why: The Mamluk army defeated the Mongols in Palestine in 1260.

wrong.1: The Song were in China and fell in 1279.
wrong.2: The Byzantines did not fight at Ain Jalut.
